thread.title: Charting a corrective bounce, S&P 500 reclaims 200-day average

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Charting a corrective bounce, S&P 500 reclaims 200-day average
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Technically speaking, the major U.S. benchmarks have reversed from multi-month lows, rising in the wake of an aggressive October downdraft.
In the process, the S&P 500 has reclaimed its 200-day moving average, currently 2,767, a move placing its former range top (2,802) firmly within view. The pending retest from underneath should be a useful bull-bear gauge.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, +1.72% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
See Also The Man Behind the World's Biggest Private-Equity Insolvency × As illustrated, the S&P has reversed from three-month lows.
Tactically, the 200-day moving average, currently 2,767, is followed by resistance broadly spanning from 2,785 to 2,802. Recall that the March peak (2,802) formerly defined a five-month range top.
Similarly, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +1.68% has rallied from three-month lows.
In its case, the 25,400 mark remains an inflection point, matching the August gap (25,401) and the June peak (25,402).
Additional overhead matches the Oct. 10 close (25,598), the session punctuating last week’s 832-point singe-day plunge, better illustrated on the daily chart.
Against this backdrop, the Nasdaq Composite COMP, +2.32% has reversed from five-month lows.
The rally attempt was initially capped by 200-day moving average, currently 7,509, an area the Nasdaq has cleared early Tuesday.
The index is traversing recently less-charted territory, better illustrated below.
Widening the view to six months adds perspective.
On this wider view, the Nasdaq is digesting a damaging October downdraft.
To reiterate, the 200-day moving average (7,509) has capped the initial rally attempt, though the Nasdaq has ventured higher early Tuesday. A close atop the 200-day would mark technical progress.
On further strength, resistance broadly spans from about 7,595 to 7,637, the latter matching the March peak.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has plunged as much as 2,053 points, or 7.6%, from a record high established Oct. 3.
The October low (24,899) has thus far registered slightly atop the 2017 peak (24,876).
Tactically, a near-term inflection point (25,598), detailed previously, is followed by more distant gap resistance (25,882). The latter underpinned the September range, and a close higher would stabilize the Dow’s backdrop.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has reversed from three-month lows amid still relatively technical price action.
Recall that the October low (2,710) has matched support at the March gap (2,709.8).
Separately, consider that last week’s close (2,767) almost precisely matched the 200-day moving average, currently 2,767.
The bigger picture As detailed above, the U.S. benchmarks have reversed from multi-month lows, rising in the wake of a technically damaging October downdraft.
Tactically, the 200-day moving average initially capped the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite, areas both benchmarks have cleared early Tuesday.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF IWM, +2.26% is digesting a plunge to five-month lows.
Tactically, near-term resistance (156.56), detailed previously, is under siege early Tuesday. This is followed by the 160.00 inflection point, and the slightly more distant 200-day moving average, currently 161.08.
Similarly, the SPDR S&P MidCap 400 is digesting a downdraft to five-month lows.
In its case, near-term overhead (346.79) is followed by the 200-day moving average, currently 355.20.
Combined, the small- and mid-cap benchmarks remain near-term oversold, and a corrective bounce is underway.
Still, both benchmarks have technically signaled a primary trend shift. A relatively swift reversal atop the 200-day moving average would mark a step toward repairing recent damage. The pending retest from underneath is worth tracking.
Looking elsewhere, the SPDR Trust S&P 500 remains comparably stronger than the small- and mid-caps. Still, the October downdraft has been fueled by a sustained volume spike, inflicting technical damage.
From current levels, the 200-day moving average, currently 276.40, is followed by resistance broadly spanning from 278.30 to 279.50.
Against this backdrop, the S&P 500 is digesting an aggressive October plunge to three-month lows. The initial downdraft was directionally sharp, violating the 50- and 200-day moving average across consecutive sessions.
By comparison, the initial rally attempt registered as flat, though it has accelerated early Tuesday.
Tactically, notable overhead matches the 200-day moving average, currently 2,767, a level matching last week’s close. The S&P has ventured higher intraday, though as always, it’s the close that matters.
This is followed by the former range top, an area broadly spanning from 2,787 to 2,802. The March peak (2,802) formerly capped a jagged five-month range.
As always, it’s not just what the S&P 500 does, it’s how it does it. A strong-volume rally atop the 2,800 area — fueled by firmly bullish market breadth — would place the index on firmer technical ground.
But pending such a move, the S&P 500’s intermediate-term technical bias remains bearish. The prevailing rally attempt’s quality, across the next several sessions, will likely add color.
See also: Cracks surface in the bull trend, S&P 500 nails major support.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Drilling down further, the SPDR Gold Shares ETF GLD, +0.09% has broken out, rising amid an October flight to safety.
Specifically, the shares have knifed atop trendline resistance, reaching 10-week highs amid a volume spike.
Though near-term extended, and due to consolidate, the shares remain attractive on a pullback. Well-defined support matches the breakout point (114.70) and is followed by the 50-day moving average, currently 113.55. The rally attempt is intact barring a violation.
Meanwhile, the VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF GDX, +0.00% has also come to life, rising amid surging gold prices.
Technically, the group has knifed from a head-and-shoulders bottom, reaching two-month highs.
Here again, the group is near-term extended, though a pullback toward support would offer an attractive entry. Tactically, the breakout point (19.25) is closely followed by the 50-day moving average, currently 18.85, and the group’s recovery attempt is intact barring a violation.
Traditional sector leaders digest the October technical damage Moving to the U.S. sub-sector backdrop, the traditional sector leaders — the transports, financials and technology sector — are digesting the October downdraft.
To start, the transports IYT, +1.80% have staged an aggressive October downdraft, plunging to three-month lows.
By comparison, the initial rally attempt has registered as flat, fueled by decreased volume.
Tactically, the 200-day moving average closely matches the group’s former range top, circa 195, and a close higher would mark a step toward stabilization. The pending retest from underneath should be a useful bull-bear gauge.
Meanwhile, the Financial Select Sector SPDR XLF, +1.32% has plunged from its former range, tagging 11-month lows.
The downdraft originates from the 50- and 200-day moving averages, placing major support under siege, an area better illustrated on the three-year chart.
Moreover, the group has not responded to a recent solid batch of influential earnings reports — including those from JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup — notching three straight closes near session lows.
A rally atop the breakdown point, circa 27.60, would place the group on firmer technical ground.
Looking elsewhere, the Invesco QQQ Trust QQQ, +2.32% tracks the Nasdaq 100 Index and serves as a large-cap technology sector proxy.
The group tagged a fractional record high to start October, briefly surpassing the August peak by one penny.
The subsequent downturn has been fueled by a sustained volume spike, placing the 200-day moving average, currently 171.70, under siege.
As detailed previously, a rally atop the March peak (175.21) would mark an early step toward stabilization.
Charting broadly-based damage beyond the sector leaders Beyond the sector leaders, the October downdraft has inflicted broadly-based damage. Three additional groups exemplify the backdrop.
To start, the Materials Select Sector SPDR XLB, +1.27% has fallen off a cliff, reaching 16-month lows amid a sustained volume increase.
By comparison, the initial rally attempt has registered as flat, fueled by decreased volume.
Though still deeply oversold at current levels, and due a corrective bounce, the group has asserted a bearish longer-term bias, also illustrated on the three-year chart . Tactically, the breakdown point (57.00) pivots to resistance, and a close higher would strengthen the backdrop.
Similarly, the VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF SMH, +2.77% has broken down, plunging from trendline support matching the major moving averages.
Tactically, gap resistance (99.30) is followed by the firmer breakdown point (100.80). An eventual close higher would place the brakes on bearish momentum.
More broadly, consider the pending death cross, or bearish 50-day/200-day moving average crossover.
Finally, the SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF KRE, -0.21% has plunged to 11-month lows.
The downdraft punctuates a failed retest of the breakdown point (60.50) and has dovetailed with a bearish 50-day/200-day moving average crossover. Tactically, a close atop near-term resistance (58.60) would mark an early step toward stabilization.
Summing up the sector backdrop Combined, the October market downdraft has inflicted broadly-based U.S. sub-sector damage. Though a corrective bounce is overdue, and currently underway, an extended basing period would be expected before the next durable leg higher. The quality of the prevailing rally attempt will likely add color.
